memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Every skilled woman spun with her hands and brought what she had spun - blue, purple or scarlet yarn or fine linen. And all the women who were willing and had the skill spun the goat hair." - Exod 35:25-26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
These two verses honour work that history usually forgets.

Spinning goat hair was hard, rough, unglamorous labour. It produced the outer covering of the tabernacle — the layer everyone saw from outside, and the layer nobody admired. Others spun fine linen in blue and purple, work of real beauty and precision.

God's Word records both. Not the names, but the work — permanently, in Scripture, thousands of years later.

Notice the two things joined here: willingness and skill. Skill without willingness helps no one; willingness without developed skill can only go so far. These women had both. They had learned a craft, probably over years, and when God's work needed it, they gave it.

There is real encouragement here for anyone whose service is invisible. The mother teaching her children Scripture at home. The person who cleans the church building. The one who prays for missionaries nobody else remembers. God sees work that no one photographs, and He is not unjust; He will not forget your work and the love you have shown Him (Heb 6:10).

Develop what you can do. Then hold it loosely enough that God can use it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What skill could you develop further in order to serve God better?
2. Does invisible service discourage you or free you?
3. Who around you is doing unseen work you could thank this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You see the work no one else notices. Take my hands and my hours and use them for Your purposes. Amen.
